items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma stating that a universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S is quasi-compact (source lines 1684-1688). The argument is a full constructive proof, not a citation: after the reduction to Y = Spec(B) through the local criterion for quasi-compactness, it covers X by quasi-compact open subspaces X_i obtained from an affine open covering of a surjective etale U -> X, builds the reduced closed subspace Z of T x_Y X with |Z| = |T x_Y X| minus the union of the |T_i x_Y X_i| for T = Spec(B[a_i]) and T_i = D(a_i), and then shows f_T(|Z|) is not closed. The non-routine step is the choice of the point y over which no affine neighbourhood V has X_V quasi-compact, together with the finite set J of variables occurring in a hypothetical g vanishing on f_T(|Z|): from these it produces a point x in |X_V| outside the X_j for j in J and a point t' of T over v with t' not in V(g) and t' in V(a_i) for i not in J, contradicts f_T(|Z|) contained in V(g).
